correctness.rationale: Write the exponent bit sets of \(p^a q^b\) as \(A,B\), so the number of infinitary components is \(J=|A|+|B|\) and the denominator factors are \(p^{2^i}+1\) and \(q^{2^j}+1\). For odd \(p\), distinct \(p^{2^i}+1\) have gcd \(2\); every selected index \(i\ge1\) contributes an odd prime divisor, and integrality forces that divisor to be \(q\), so there can be at most one such index and \(|A|\le2\). If \(p=2\), the Fermat-type factors \(2^{2^i}+1\) are pairwise coprime odd numbers and every denominator prime must be \(q\), forcing \(|A|\le1\); the odd-prime argument gives \(|B|\le2\), hence \(J\le3\). If both primes are odd and \(J=4\), then \(A=\{0,i\}\) and \(B=\{0,j\}\) with \(i,j\ge1\). Pairwise gcd constraints force both \(p+1\) and \(q+1\) to be powers of two. But \(q\mid p^{2^i}+1\) gives \(\operatorname{ord}_q(p)=2^{i+1}\), so \(q\equiv1\pmod4\), whereas an odd prime with \(q+1\) a power of two satisfies \(q\equiv3\pmod4\), a contradiction. Thus \(J\le3\) for every two-prime infinitary harmonic integer. The published complete \(J\le3\) list is \(\{1,6,45,60,90,15925\}\), of which exactly \(6\) and \(45\) have two distinct prime factors. The bounded package computation is corroborative only.
residual_risks: The result concerns exactly two distinct prime factors and uses the published low-component classification only after proving the all-layer bound \(J\le3\).

A separate published Resultary record classifies the entire \(J=4\) layer. Neither statement supplies the structural implication that arbitrary two-prime support forces \(J\le3\), which simultaneously removes every higher component layer. Current Resultary searches for an all-layer two-prime infinitary-harmonic classification returned the \(J=4\) census and different harmonic notions but no equivalent support theorem.
